hints: Follow the chain one arrow at a time, each reagent tells you the functional group change to expect.
LiAlH4 reduces propanoic acid all the way to a primary alcohol, so compound X is propan-1-ol.
Dehydrate that alcohol to an alkene, then hydrate it again with steam and acid, and think about where the OH adds by Markovnikov's rule.
walkthrough:
**Reduce the carboxylic acid to find X**

Great start, LiAlH4 is a very strong reducing agent. It reduces a carboxylic acid all the way to a primary alcohol.

Chemical change:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
So compound X is propan-1-ol.

**Dehydrate the alcohol to find Y**

Next, concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ dehydrates an alcohol by removing water. A primary alcohol like propan-1-ol forms an alkene.

Chemical change:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So compound Y is propene.

**Hydrate the alkene to find Z**

Finally, steam over $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ adds water across the C=C bond. This is electrophilic addition and follows Markovnikov's rule.

Chemical change:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$$
The H adds to the end carbon with more H atoms, and OH adds to the middle carbon with fewer H atoms.

**Identify the major product**

The product is a secondary alcohol with the OH on carbon 2. That is propan-2-ol, which is the major product Z.

options.A: Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a ketone. No oxidising agent is used in this sequence, LiAlH4 is a reducing agent and the other steps are dehydration then hydration, so a carbonyl is never formed.
options.B: Propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$, is compound Y, not Z. It is tempting to stop after dehydration with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, but Y then undergoes hydration with steam to give Z.
options.C: Propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, is compound X, not Z. It is a common trap to think hydration of propene simply reverses dehydration to give back the same primary alcohol, but Markovnikov addition puts the OH on the middle carbon.
options.D: Propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, is correct. X is propan-1-ol, Y is propene, and Markovnikov hydration of propene adds OH to carbon 2 to give the secondary alcohol as the major product.
